s: Under Article 54 of the Constitution of India, which one of the following is included in the electoral college for the election of the President?
o: Nominated members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry
Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry
Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament
Elected members of the Legislative Councils of the States
x: The electoral college includes elected MPs and elected MLAs of the States, Delhi and Puducherry. Nominated members and members of Legislative Councils are excluded.
tq: Distinguish elected members of eligible Houses from nominated members and Legislative Council members.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: A Chief Minister who is a member of the Legislative Council of a State, rather than its Legislative Assembly, is entitled to
o: not vote in the election of the President
vote only if nominated by the Governor
vote in the election of the President by virtue of being the Chief Minister
vote only in the election of the Vice-President
x: Only elected members of State Legislative Assemblies form part of the Presidential electoral college. Membership of a Legislative Council does not confer this right, even on a Chief Minister.
tq: Apply the precise constitutional distinction between the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the electoral college for the election of the President:
1. Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament are excluded.
2. Members of State Legislative Councils are excluded.
3. Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry are included.
4. Elected members of all Union Territory Legislative Assemblies are included.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Constitution specifically includes Delhi and Puducherry, while Union Territories without Assemblies do not participate.
tq: Find the overbroad statement by separating the named Union Territories from all other Union Territories.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: The election of the President of India is held by
o: direct voting through universal adult franchise and open ballot
simple majority voting by elected MPs and MLAs
proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and open ballot
proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot
x: Article 55(3) prescribes proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and voting by secret ballot.
tq: Test the paired constitutional features together: STV and secret ballot.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: The system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote used in the election of the President was borrowed from the Constitution of
x: The Presidential election method of proportional representation by single transferable vote was borrowed from Ireland.
tq: Use the source-country association for a distinctive constitutional device.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: The constitutional objective of maintaining uniformity among the States and parity between the States as a whole and the Union in the Presidential election is secured through
o: direct election by the people of India
equal vote value for every elector irrespective of the House represented
nomination of an equal number of electors by every State
differential value assigned to MLA and MP votes
x: Article 55(1) achieves these principles by assigning vote values to MLAs based on State population and distributing the aggregate MLA vote value among elected MPs.
tq: Connect the constitutional objective with the mechanism that gives effect to it.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: The value of the vote of an elected member of a State Legislative Assembly is calculated by the formula:
o: Number of elected MLAs divided by State population, multiplied by 1,000
State population divided by the number of elected MLAs, multiplied by 1/1,000
State population divided by the number of elected MLAs, multiplied by 1,000
State population divided by the total number of members of both Houses of Parliament
x: The value of an MLA's vote is calculated as (population of the State divided by the number of elected MLAs) multiplied by 1/1000.
tq: Read the formula carefully and distinguish multiplication by 1/1000 from multiplication by 1000.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: The value of the vote of an elected Member of Parliament in the election of the President is determined by
o: multiplying the value of the highest-valued MLA vote by the number of States
dividing the total value of all MLA votes by the total number of elected MPs
dividing the total number of elected MPs by the total value of all MLA votes
assigning an identical value fixed by Parliament to every MP
x: The value of an MP's vote equals the total value of all votes of elected MLAs divided by the total number of elected MPs.
tq: Identify the correct numerator and denominator in the constitutional calculation.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: For determining the value of votes in the Presidential election, the population of the States is presently taken on the basis of the
x: The population base for calculating the value of votes is the 1971 Census, which has been frozen for this purpose.
tq: Test the frozen census base rather than the latest available census.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: The population base used for calculating the value of votes in the Presidential election is to remain frozen until
o: a constitutional amendment made after every Census
x: The 1971 Census base remains frozen until the first Census conducted after 2026, as provided through the constitutional arrangement referred to in the 84th Amendment.
tq: Use the end-point of a constitutional freeze instead of substituting a recent census year.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional position regarding disputes connected with the election of the President?
o: They are decided by the Election Commission of India alone.
They are decided by Parliament through a joint sitting.
They are decided by the Council of Ministers.
They are decided only by the Supreme Court.
x: Under Article 71, disputes relating to the election of the President are decided only by the Supreme Court.
tq: Match the constitutional dispute with the authority expressly entrusted to decide it.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: If the election of the President is subsequently declared void, which one of the following is the effect on acts performed by the President before such declaration?
o: All such acts automatically become void.
Their validity is decided by the outgoing President.
Only financial acts remain valid; all other acts become void.
x: Article 71 protects acts done by the President in the performance of duties before the election is declared void; those acts do not become invalid merely because of the declaration.
tq: Separate the validity of past official acts from the validity of the election itself.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s: A vacancy in the electoral college for the election of the President
o: does not by itself constitute a ground for challenging the election
can be challenged only if caused by resignation of an MP
requires postponement of the election until the vacancy is filled
x: Article 71(4) provides that the election of the President cannot be called in question on the ground of any vacancy in the electoral college.
tq: Identify the constitutional exception that prevents a vacancy from defeating the election.
sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Article)
A. Article 52
B. Article 54
C. Article 60
D. Article 71

List-II (Subject)
1. Oath or affirmation of the President
2. Election disputes
3. There shall be a President of India
4. Electoral college for election of the President
x: Article 52 provides for the office of the President, Article 54 concerns the electoral college, Article 60 concerns the oath or affirmation, and Article 71 concerns election disputes.
tq: Start with the sure article-subject pairs and eliminate codes with a misplaced constitutional provision.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 56 — Term of office of the President
Article 59 — Conditions of the President's office
Article 62 — Oath or affirmation of the President
x: Article 62 deals with the time of election to fill a vacancy in the office of the President. The oath or affirmation is dealt with by Article 60.
tq: Find the single article-subject swap among closely placed provisions.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s: The constitutional provision relating to the impeachment of the President of India is contained in Article
x: Article 61 lays down the procedure for impeachment of the President.
tq: Use the article-number sequence and distinguish impeachment from qualifications, conditions and vacancy.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President.
2. Article 56 deals with the term of office of the President and resignation to the Vice-President.
3. Article 58 lays down the qualifications for election as President.
4. Article 60 deals with the President's eligibility for re-election.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: Article 60 concerns the oath or affirmation, while eligibility for re-election is dealt with by Article 57.
tq: Catch the adjacent-article substitution between re-election and oath provisions.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s: Which one of the following correctly gives the sequence of subjects covered by Articles 52, 53, 54 and 55?
o: President; executive power; election; manner of election
Executive power; President; manner of election; election disputes
Qualifications; executive power; election; term of office
x: Article 52 provides for the President, Article 53 vests Union executive power in the President, Article 54 concerns the electoral college, and Article 55 prescribes the manner of election.
tq: Follow the consecutive article sequence from the office itself to its election method.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 65 — Vice-President to act as President
Article 72 — Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
x: Article 65 provides for the Vice-President acting as President in specified circumstances. Article 72 concerns pardon, Article 74 concerns aid and advice by the Council of Ministers, and Article 76 concerns the Attorney General.
tq: Use neighbouring constitutional provisions as distractors and identify the exact article-subject pairing.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s: Articles 52 to 78 of the Constitution of India constitute
o: Part V, Chapter I dealing with the Union Executive
Part VI, Chapter I dealing with the State Executive
Part III dealing with Fundamental Rights
Part V, Chapter II dealing with Parliament
x: Articles 52 to 78 fall under Part V, Chapter I, which deals with the Union Executive.
tq: Distinguish the Part and Chapter classification from the adjacent chapter on Parliament.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s:
Which of the following are legislative functions of the President of India?
1. Summoning and proroguing both Houses of Parliament
2. Dissolving the Lok Sabha
3. Summoning a joint sitting of Parliament
4. Sending messages to either House of Parliament
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The President can summon and prorogue Parliament, dissolve the Lok Sabha, summon a joint sitting, and send messages to either House. A joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
tq: Check whether all listed functions belong to the President's legislative field rather than treating the joint sitting as a parliamentary initiative alone.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s: The President addresses Parliament under Articles 86 and 87 on, among other occasions,
o: every session before the presentation of the Union Budget
only the last session of every year
only a joint sitting convened during a constitutional emergency
the first session after each general election and the first session of each year
x: The President addresses both Houses assembled together at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year under Articles 86 and 87.
tq: Distinguish constitutionally specified occasions from routine parliamentary sessions.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s: A Bill passed by Parliament cannot become law unless it receives the assent of the President because
o: the President is not a component of Parliament
the President is a part of Parliament under Article 79
the President alone introduces every Bill in Parliament
the President presides over both Houses of Parliament
x: Article 79 makes the President a part of Parliament. Consequently, a Bill passed by Parliament requires Presidential assent to become law.
tq: Link the constitutional composition of Parliament with the assent requirement.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s:
Under Article 240, the President may make regulations for which of the following Union Territories?
1. Andaman and Nicobar Islands
2. Lakshadweep
3. Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
4. Puducherry when its Legislative Assembly is suspended or dissolved
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Article 240 covers the listed Union Territories, including Puducherry when its Legislative Assembly is suspended or dissolved. The President administers Union Territories through administrators.
tq: Test the complete territorial list and the special condition attached to Puducherry.
sec: Articles 52-62 number game

s: Which one of the following is NOT a constitutional qualification for election as the President of India?
o: Qualification for election to the Lok Sabha
Membership of either House of Parliament
x: A presidential candidate must be an Indian citizen, at least 35 years old, qualified for election to the Lok Sabha and must not hold an office of profit. Membership of Parliament is not required.
tq: Find the option that confuses an eligibility qualification with a condition that is not prescribed.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s: A person who holds an office of profit under the Union Government is generally disqualified from contesting the election to the office of the President because of which constitutional provision?
x: Article 58 prescribes the qualifications for election as President, including the condition that the person must not hold an office of profit under the Union, a State or a local or other authority.
tq: Use the article-number clue to distinguish qualifications from term, office conditions and oath.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the term and re-election of the President of India:
1. The President holds office for five years.
2. The President is eligible for re-election.
3. The Constitution limits a person to two terms as President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The President holds office for five years and may be re-elected. The Constitution does not prescribe any limit on the number of terms.
tq: Reject the familiar but unsupported two-term limitation and retain the two directly stated provisions.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s: The emoluments of the President of India are primarily dealt with in which of the following constitutional arrangements?
o: They are fixed by the Union Cabinet and listed in the First Schedule.
They are fixed by Parliament by law and listed in the Second Schedule.
They are fixed annually by the Finance Commission and listed in the Fourth Schedule.
They are fixed by the Supreme Court and included in the Third Schedule.
x: The emoluments of the President are fixed by Parliament by law and are listed in the Second Schedule. They cannot be diminished during the term of office.
tq: Match the financial detail with the correct Schedule and authority instead of relying on a neighbouring Schedule.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the emoluments of the President is correct?
o: They cannot be diminished during the President's term of office.
They are determined by the Chief Justice of India.
They may be reduced by Parliament during the President's term in the national interest.
They are determined exclusively by the Council of Ministers.
x: Although Parliament fixes the emoluments by law, they cannot be diminished during the President's term of office.
tq: Focus on the constitutional protection against diminution rather than on the authority that fixes the emoluments.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s: The oath of office to the President of India is administered by the:
o: Chief Justice of India or, in his absence, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court
x: Under Article 60, the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India; in his absence, it is administered by the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court.
tq: Apply the who-would-do-this-job method to distinguish the oath-taking authority from other constitutional functionaries.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s: Which expression forms part of the President's oath under Article 60?
o: To preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law
To faithfully execute the office of the Prime Minister
To protect the Constitution, Parliament and the Supreme Court exclusively
To uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India alone
x: The President swears to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law, and to devote himself or herself to the service and well-being of the people of India.
tq: Test the exact constitutional wording and reject look-alike phrases that alter or narrow it.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s: If the President of India resigns from office, the resignation letter is addressed to the:
x: The President resigns by writing to the Vice-President. The Vice-President then informs the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
tq: Trace the constitutional communication chain and identify the immediate recipient rather than the person subsequently informed.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional position of the President:
1. The President cannot be a member of either House of Parliament or a State Legislature.
2. The official residence of the President is provided rent-free.
3. The emoluments of the President may be diminished during the term if Parliament so decides.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The President cannot be a member of any legislature and is entitled to an official residence rent-free. The emoluments cannot be diminished during the term, making statement 3 false.
tq: Identify the reversed protection in statement 3 while retaining the two true conditions of the office.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s: Which of the following correctly describes the protection available to the President under Article 361?
o: Official acts of the President may always be examined through criminal proceedings during the term.
The President is immune from all civil suits for an unlimited period.
The President may be arrested during the term after approval by Parliament.
No criminal proceedings can be instituted against the President during the term, while a civil suit requires two months' notice.
x: Article 361 protects the President from criminal proceedings during the term and provides immunity for official acts. A civil suit requires two months' prior notice; the immunity from civil proceedings is not unlimited.
tq: Separate criminal immunity, protection for official acts and the notice requirement instead of treating them as one absolute immunity.
sec: Qualifications, term, re-election, salary, oath, resignation

s: The sole constitutional ground for impeachment of the President of India is:
o: Loss of majority in the Lok Sabha
Disobedience of the advice of the Council of Ministers
x: Article 61 provides impeachment only for violation of the Constitution. The other grounds are not specified as grounds for presidential impeachment.
tq: Recall the exact constitutional ground and avoid substituting political or administrative misconduct.
sec: Impeachment - Article 61

s: Which one of the following statements about the use of the term “impeachment” in the constitutional context is correct?
o: It is used for the removal of the President, judges of the Supreme Court and the Vice-President alike.
It is used for every constitutional office-holder removed by Parliament.
It is used only for the President; judges and the Vice-President are removed through procedures described as removal.
It is used only for the Vice-President and Governors.
x: In the constitutional terminology stated here, impeachment is used only for the President. Judges and the Vice-President are described as being removed.
tq: Discriminate between closely associated constitutional terms rather than treating impeachment as a generic word for removal.
sec: Impeachment - Article 61

s: A charge for impeachment of the President may be initiated in:
o: A joint sitting of both Houses only
x: The impeachment charge may be initiated in either House of Parliament. It is not confined to one particular House or to a joint sitting.
tq: Test the constitutional choice between either House, one specified House and a joint sitting.
sec: Impeachment - Article 61

s: For initiating a charge of impeachment against the President, the notice must be signed by at least:
o: One-tenth of the members of the concerned House
One-half of the members of the concerned House
One-sixth of the members of the concerned House
One-fourth of the members of the concerned House
x: The notice of the impeachment charge must be signed by at least one-fourth of the members of the House in which the charge is initiated, and fourteen days' notice is required.
tq: Use the fraction as the decisive numerical clue and distinguish it from the voting threshold at a later stage.
sec: Impeachment - Article 61

s: The minimum notice period required before moving a charge for impeachment of the President is:
x: The notice for initiating the charge must be given fourteen days in advance and must be signed by at least one-fourth of the members of the concerned House.
tq: Separate the notice period from the two-thirds voting requirement and identify the exact number of days.
sec: Impeachment - Article 61

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the impeachment procedure:
1. The initiating House must pass the charge by a majority of two-thirds of its total membership.
2. The other House investigates the charge.
3. The President has the right to appear and to be represented during the investigation.
4. The other House must also pass the charge by two-thirds of its total membership for impeachment to take effect.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements correctly describe Article 61. Both Houses must approve the charge by a two-thirds majority of their total membership, with investigation by the other House and an opportunity for the President to appear or be represented.
tq: Read the procedure sequentially: notice, initiating vote, investigation, representation and final vote.
sec: Impeachment - Article 61

s:
Which of the following correctly represents participation in the impeachment of the President?
1. Elected members of the Lok Sabha participate.
2. Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha participate.
3. Elected Members of Legislative Assemblies participate.
4. Nominated members of Parliament participate.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament participate in impeachment. Elected MLAs of the States, Delhi and Puducherry do not participate.
tq: Use the composition distinction: the presidential electoral college and the impeachment forum are not identical.
sec: Impeachment - Article 61

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the history of presidential impeachment in India?
o: One President has been impeached by the Rajya Sabha.
Two Presidents have been impeached by joint sittings of Parliament.
No President of India has been impeached so far.
The first President was impeached but later reinstated.
x: No President of India has been impeached so far.
tq: Identify the precise historical status and reject options that invent a completed impeachment.
sec: Impeachment - Article 61

s: Which one of the following is a legislative power of the President of India?
o: Appointing all Members of Legislative Assemblies
Vetoing judicial decisions of the Supreme Court
Nominating twelve members to the Rajya Sabha
x: The President nominates twelve members to the Rajya Sabha. Summoning and proroguing Parliament, dissolving the Lok Sabha and promulgating ordinances are also legislative powers.
tq: Match the power with the correct constitutional institution and reject powers assigned to the judiciary or State legislatures.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the legislative powers of the President:
1. The President summons and prorogues Parliament.
2. The President may dissolve the Lok Sabha.
3. A Money Bill requires the President's prior recommendation.
4. The President promulgates ordinances under Article 123.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four are legislative powers or functions of the President. Article 123 specifically empowers the President to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session.
tq: Check each statement against the legislative cluster and use the all-inclusive option only when every item fits.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s:
The President's prior recommendation is required for the introduction of which of the following?
1. A Money Bill
2. A Bill under Article 3 affecting the area, boundaries or name of a State
3. Every Private Member's Bill in the Lok Sabha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Prior recommendation is required for a Money Bill and for a Bill under Article 3. It is not required for every Private Member's Bill.
tq: Spot the overbroad word “every” and distinguish special constitutional introductions from ordinary legislative business.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 240 — Regulations for certain Union Territories
Article 143 — Consultation with the Supreme Court
Article 360 — Appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General
x: Article 360 concerns financial emergency. The Comptroller and Auditor General is appointed by the President under Article 148, whereas Articles 123, 143 and 240 correspond to the powers stated in the other pairs.
tq: Find the wrong article-power pair by matching each article with its constitutional subject.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s: The advice tendered by the Supreme Court to the President under Article 143 is:
o: Binding only during a financial emergency
Binding after approval by the Rajya Sabha
x: Under Article 143, the President may consult the Supreme Court, but the advice given by the Court is not binding.
tq: Discriminate between consultation and compulsory compliance by focusing on the legal effect of the advice.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Article 72 — Pardoning power
2. Article 143 — Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
3. Article 352 — National Emergency
4. Article 356 — Financial Emergency
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Articles 72, 143 and 352 correspond respectively to the pardoning power, consultation with the Supreme Court and National Emergency. Article 356 concerns failure of constitutional machinery in a State; Financial Emergency is under Article 360.
tq: Use article-subject matching and catch the swapped emergency provisions in statement 4.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s:
Arrange the following functions in the order of the constitutional articles associated with them, beginning with the lowest article number:
A. Financial Emergency
B. Pardoning power
C. Ordinance-making power
D. Consultation with the Supreme Court
x: The relevant articles are Article 72 for pardoning power, Article 123 for ordinances, Article 143 for consultation with the Supreme Court and Article 360 for Financial Emergency. Therefore the order is B, C, D, A.
tq: Convert each function into its article number and arrange the numbers rather than the functions by memory alone.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s: Which one of the following is a financial power of the President of India?
o: Fixing the repo rate for the Reserve Bank of India
Advancing money from the Contingency Fund of India
x: The President can authorise advances from the Contingency Fund of India. The Budget is laid before Parliament in the President's name, and recommendations are required for Money Bills and demands for grants.
tq: Identify the function that belongs to the President's constitutional financial role without assigning executive or monetary-policy powers to that office.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s: Which one of the following correctly states the President's role in the administration of Union Territories?
o: The President has no constitutional role in the administration of Union Territories.
The President administers all Union Territories directly through the Supreme Court.
The President administers Union Territories through administrators and may make regulations for certain Union Territories under Article 240.
The President administers Union Territories only through State Governors.
x: The President administers Union Territories through administrators and may make regulations for certain Union Territories under Article 240.
tq: Match the office with the correct administrative channel and the specific article-based power.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched with the constitutional basis of appointment?
1. Comptroller and Auditor General — Article 148
2. Governors — Article 155
3. Attorney General — Article 76
4. Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners — Article 324
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four pairings are correct: Articles 148, 155, 76 and 324 respectively concern the CAG, Governors, Attorney General, and the Election Commission.
tq: Verify every article-authority pair individually before accepting the comprehensive combination.
sec: Powers of the President - statement based

s: The constitutional arrangement under which the Council of Ministers aids and advises the President is provided in:
x: Article 74(1) provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President.
tq: Match the institutional relationship with its specific constitutional article.
sec: Position - constitutional head, Article 74

s: Which one of the following best describes the constitutional position of the President and the Prime Minister?
o: The President is the real executive and the Prime Minister is the nominal executive.
The President is the nominal or de jure executive, while the Prime Minister is the real or de facto executive.
The Prime Minister is the constitutional head and the President is only a ceremonial officer without executive status.
Both are independent real executives with equal authority in all matters.
x: The President is the nominal or de jure executive, while the Prime Minister, heading the Council of Ministers, functions as the real or de facto executive.
tq: Use the nominal-versus-real executive distinction and reject the reversal of roles.
sec: Position - constitutional head, Article 74

s:
Consider the following statements about Article 74:
1. The 42nd Constitutional Amendment made the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President.
2. The 44th Constitutional Amendment enabled the President to return the advice once for reconsideration.
3. After reconsideration, the President may permanently reject the advice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 42nd Amendment made the advice binding. The 44th Amendment allows the President to return it once for reconsideration, but after reconsideration the President must act according to the advice; statement 3 is false.
tq: Track the amendment sequence and identify the false final consequence of reconsideration.
sec: Position - constitutional head, Article 74

s:
Assertion (A): The President may return the advice of the Council of Ministers for reconsideration once.
Reason (R): The 44th Constitutional Amendment introduced this limited power of reconsideration.
Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true, and the 44th Constitutional Amendment is the reason the President acquired the power to return the advice once for reconsideration. After reconsideration, the advice is binding.
tq: Check whether the constitutional amendment stated in the Reason directly accounts for the power asserted.
sec: Position - constitutional head, Article 74

s: Under Article 74(2), which of the following is correct regarding the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers?
o: The advice tendered to the President cannot be inquired into by any court.
The advice becomes public automatically after being tendered.
Any court may inquire into the advice if the President requests it.
Only the Supreme Court may inquire into the advice.
x: Article 74(2) provides that the question, if any, and what advice was tendered by Ministers to the President cannot be inquired into by any court.
tq: Identify the constitutional bar on judicial inquiry and reject options that create exceptions not provided here.
sec: Position - constitutional head, Article 74

s: Under Article 62 of the Constitution, an election to fill a vacancy in the office of the President caused by the expiration of the term of office shall be completed:
o: Within one year after the expiry of the term
Within six months after the expiry of the term
Only after the outgoing President vacates office
Before the expiration of the term
x: Article 62(1) requires the election to be completed before the expiration of the President’s term.
tq: Test the precise time limit rather than confusing expiry-of-term vacancies with casual vacancies.
sec: Vacancy - election time limit and acting President  [APPSC]

s: In the event of the death, resignation, removal, disqualification or void election of the President, the election to fill the vacancy must be held within:
x: For a vacancy arising from a cause other than expiry of the term, Article 62 requires the election within six months.
tq: Separate the six-month rule for casual vacancies from the before-expiry rule.
sec: Vacancy - election time limit and acting President  [APPSC]

s: A person elected to fill a casual vacancy in the office of the President holds office for:
o: Three years from the date of election
A full term of five years from entering office
The unexpired portion of the predecessor’s term
x: The President elected to fill a casual vacancy receives a fresh full five-year term.
tq: Watch for the common trap of treating a casual-vacancy successor as an interim office-holder.
sec: Vacancy - election time limit and acting President  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the outgoing President:
1. The outgoing President continues in office until the successor enters upon office.
2. This continuation applies even when the election is completed before the expiry of the term.
3. The outgoing President’s term automatically ends on the date on which the election result is declared.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct under Article 56. Statement 3 is false because declaration of the result alone does not terminate the outgoing President’s office.
tq: Identify the one statement that wrongly substitutes declaration of result for assumption of office.
sec: Vacancy - election time limit and acting President  [APPSC]

s: When the Vice-President acts as President under Article 65, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Vice-President continues to preside over the Rajya Sabha while acting as President
The Deputy Chairman presides over the Rajya Sabha during that period
The Rajya Sabha is automatically dissolved
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the Rajya Sabha
x: While acting as President, the Vice-President ceases to perform the functions of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; the Deputy Chairman presides.
tq: Use the role-separation trap: a person acting as President cannot simultaneously perform the Chairman’s functions in the Rajya Sabha.
sec: Vacancy - election time limit and acting President  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a vacancy in the office of the Vice-President from a vacancy in the office of the President?
o: A Vice-Presidential vacancy is filled only by nomination
A Vice-Presidential vacancy must also be filled within six months
A Vice-Presidential vacancy cannot arise by resignation
A Vice-Presidential vacancy has no six-month deadline under Article 68
x: Unlike a casual vacancy in the office of the President, Article 68 does not prescribe a six-month deadline for filling a Vice-Presidential vacancy.
tq: Discriminate between the similar-looking vacancy provisions of Articles 62 and 68.
sec: Vacancy - election time limit and acting President  [APPSC]

s: If the offices of both the President and Vice-President are vacant, who acts as President first?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: When both offices are vacant, the Chief Justice of India acts as President; in the absence of the CJI, the senior-most Supreme Court judge performs the function.
tq: Test the constitutional succession sequence by identifying the first office-holder in the chain.
sec: Vacancy - election time limit and acting President  [APPSC]

s: All doubts and disputes relating to the election of the President or Vice-President are decided by:
x: Article 71 vests the Supreme Court with exclusive authority to decide doubts and disputes concerning Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections.
tq: Use the authority-identification method: distinguish the body conducting an election from the body deciding its disputes.
sec: Election disputes - Article 71  [other exams]

s:
With reference to Article 71, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court alone decides disputes concerning the election of the President and Vice-President.
2. Parliament may regulate matters connected with such elections other than the adjudication of election disputes.
3. An election can be challenged merely because there is a vacancy in the electoral college.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 71(4) bars a challenge on the ground of a vacancy in the electoral college.
tq: Find the exception hidden in the negative statement about vacancies in the electoral college.
sec: Election disputes - Article 71  [other exams]

s: The 39th Constitutional Amendment and the 44th Constitutional Amendment had what effect on Presidential election disputes?
o: The 39th Amendment vested the disputes in Parliament and the 44th retained that arrangement
The 39th Amendment removed the Supreme Court’s power and the 44th Amendment restored it
The 39th Amendment created the power and the 44th Amendment abolished it
Both Amendments transferred the power to the Election Commission
x: The 39th Amendment of 1975 took away the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction over these disputes, while the 44th Amendment of 1978 restored it.
tq: Link each Amendment to its opposite constitutional effect instead of relying on the later amendment alone.
sec: Election disputes - Article 71  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zakir Husain — First President from South India
Rajendra Prasad — Only President elected twice
S. Radhakrishnan — First President to die in office
M. Hidayatullah — Only President elected unopposed
x: Rajendra Prasad was the only President elected twice, in 1952 and 1957. Radhakrishnan was the first President from South India, Zakir Husain was the first to die in office, and Hidayatullah acted as President.
tq: Use the wrong-person-with-deed trap by matching each President with the correct distinction.

s: Who was the first President of India from South India and had earlier served as the first Vice-President?
x: S. Radhakrishnan, President from 1962 to 1967, was the first President from South India and had earlier been the first Vice-President.
tq: Combine two linked identifiers to distinguish a President from other holders of ‘first’ positions.
sec: Presidents of India - order and FIRSTs  [other exams]

s: Who was the first President of India to die in office?
x: Zakir Husain, who served from 1967 to 1969, was the first President of India to die in office.
tq: Test the exact sequence of similar facts concerning Presidents who died while holding office.
sec: Presidents of India - order and FIRSTs  [other exams]

s: M. Hidayatullah is remembered in the constitutional history of India as the:
o: Only Chief Justice of India to act as President
x: M. Hidayatullah was the only Chief Justice of India to act as President.
tq: Identify the unique institutional combination rather than confusing an acting President with an elected President.
sec: Presidents of India - order and FIRSTs  [other exams]

s: V.V. Giri became President after winning on the basis of:
o: A nomination by the Supreme Court
x: V.V. Giri won the 1969 Presidential election on second-preference votes.
tq: Test the distinctive election feature attached to the individual President.
sec: Presidents of India - order and FIRSTs  [other exams]

s: Who acted as President after the death of Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed?
x: After Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed died in office, B.D. Jatti acted as President.
tq: Avoid the chronology trap by separating the President who died in office from the person who acted afterward.
sec: Presidents of India - order and FIRSTs  [other exams]

s:
Consider the following statements about N. Sanjiva Reddy:
1. He was the only President elected unopposed.
2. He was from Andhra Pradesh.
3. He had earlier served as Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
4. He was the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements correctly describe N. Sanjiva Reddy, who served as President from 1977 to 1982.
tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after verifying each biographical identifier separately.
sec: Presidents of India - order and FIRSTs  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India and the only President elected twice; Pratibha Patil was the first woman President.
tq: Find the biography attached to the wrong President, a standard wrong-person-with-deed trap.
sec: Presidents of India - order and FIRSTs  [other exams]

s:
Arrange the following Presidents of India in chronological order of assuming office:
A. K.R. Narayanan
B. Pratibha Patil
C. N. Sanjiva Reddy
D. Droupadi Murmu
x: N. Sanjiva Reddy assumed office in 1977, K.R. Narayanan in 1997, Pratibha Patil in 2007 and Droupadi Murmu in 2022.
tq: Place the earliest and latest office-holders first, then resolve the two middle dates.
sec: Presidents of India - order and FIRSTs  [other exams]

s: Droupadi Murmu assumed office as the President of India on:
x: Droupadi Murmu became President on 25 July 2022 and is the first tribal President of India.
tq: Test the exact year associated with a recent constitutional office-holder rather than the sequence number alone.
sec: Presidents of India - order and FIRSTs  [other exams]

s: Which of the following forms of clemency removes both the sentence and the conviction?
x: A pardon removes the sentence as well as the conviction. Commutation substitutes a lighter punishment, remission reduces the period, and reprieve temporarily stays execution.
tq: Discriminate among closely related forms of pardoning power by their legal effect.
sec: Pardoning power - Article 72 vs 161  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its meaning?
o: Remission — reduction of the period of sentence without changing its character
Respite — removal of conviction and sentence
Reprieve — substitution of a lighter form of punishment
x: Remission reduces the period of punishment while retaining its character. Reprieve is a temporary stay, commutation substitutes a lighter punishment, and pardon removes conviction and sentence.
tq: Start from the precise meaning of one form and eliminate the swapped meanings of the other forms.
sec: Pardoning power - Article 72 vs 161  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the pardoning powers of the President and Governor:
1. The President may pardon a death sentence.
2. The Governor cannot pardon a death sentence but may suspend, remit or commute it.
3. The Governor may grant pardon in a court-martial case.
4. The President may exercise pardoning power in court-martial cases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Governor has no power to pardon a court-martial sentence.
tq: Separate the President’s wider jurisdiction over death sentences and court-martial cases from the Governor’s narrower power.
sec: Pardoning power - Article 72 vs 161  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The pardoning power of the President under Article 72 and of the Governor under Article 161 respectively relates primarily to offences against:
x: The President deals with offences against Union laws, while the Governor deals with offences against State laws.
tq: Use the Union–State jurisdiction contrast to avoid reversing the two constitutional provisions.
sec: Pardoning power - Article 72 vs 161  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The pardoning power of the President is exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers according to:
o: Epuru Sudhakar v. Government of Andhra Pradesh (2006)
x: Maru Ram (1980) established that the President exercises the pardoning power on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
tq: Match the case with its specific constitutional holding rather than grouping all pardon cases together.
sec: Pardoning power - Article 72 vs 161  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which one of the following correctly states the scope of judicial review of the President’s pardoning power?
o: It may be reviewed only for violation of a fundamental right expressly named in the order
It is completely immune from judicial review
It may be reviewed for mala fide, arbitrary or irrelevant grounds
It can be reviewed only by Parliament
x: Kehar Singh and Epuru Sudhakar recognised limited judicial review where the exercise is mala fide, arbitrary or based on irrelevant grounds.
tq: Reject the extreme-word trap in ‘completely immune’ and apply the limited-review principle.
sec: Pardoning power - Article 72 vs 161  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: An Ordinance under Article 123 may be promulgated by the President only when:
o: Either House of Parliament is not in session and immediate action is considered necessary
The Lok Sabha alone has been dissolved permanently
The Supreme Court directs the President to promulgate it
Both Houses of Parliament are in session and urgent legislation is required
x: Article 123 permits an Ordinance when Parliament is not in session and the President is satisfied that immediate action is necessary. The expression includes a situation in which either House is not in session.
tq: Focus on the exact constitutional condition and avoid the trap that both Houses must be absent simultaneously.
sec: Ordinance - Article 123, life, lapse, review cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: An Ordinance promulgated under Article 123 has the same force and effect as:
o: A resolution of either House of Parliament
An executive order of the Prime Minister
x: An Ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament, subject to the constitutional limits governing its promulgation and duration.
tq: Distinguish legal force from constitutional status: an Ordinance is not a constitutional amendment.
sec: Ordinance - Article 123, life, lapse, review cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: An Ordinance promulgated by the President ceases to operate:
o: Six weeks after Parliament reassembles, unless earlier disapproved by both Houses
Six months after promulgation in every case
Only when the President withdraws it
Six weeks after it is promulgated, irrespective of Parliament’s sittings
x: An Ordinance lapses six weeks after Parliament reassembles, or earlier if both Houses disapprove it. The President may also withdraw it at any time.
tq: Combine the normal lapse rule with the earlier-disapproval exception instead of using the maximum-life figure alone.
sec: Ordinance - Article 123, life, lapse, review cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: What is the maximum possible life of a Presidential Ordinance, assuming the constitutional conditions for its promulgation and continuation are met?
x: The maximum possible life of an Ordinance is six months plus six weeks, linked to the interval between parliamentary sessions and the post-reassembly period.
tq: Do not confuse the six-week post-reassembly period with the total maximum life.
sec: Ordinance - Article 123, life, lapse, review cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which one of the following statements about the legislative scope of a Presidential Ordinance is correct?
o: It may amend the Constitution because it has the force of an Act
Its scope is co-extensive with Parliament’s legislative power and it cannot amend the Constitution
It may legislate on any matter, including matters beyond Parliament’s competence
It can be issued only on State List subjects
x: An Ordinance can cover matters within Parliament’s legislative competence, but it cannot be used to amend the Constitution.
tq: Separate the scope of ordinary legislation from the higher power of constitutional amendment.
sec: Ordinance - Article 123, life, lapse, review cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The Governor’s power corresponding to the President’s power to promulgate Ordinances under Article 123 is provided under:
x: Article 213 confers the parallel Ordinance-making power on the Governor of a State.
tq: Discriminate between the Governor’s pardoning provision and the Governor’s Ordinance provision.
sec: Ordinance - Article 123, life, lapse, review cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which Constitutional Amendment made the President’s satisfaction in promulgating an Ordinance final, and which Amendment reversed that position?
o: 38th Amendment made it final; 44th Amendment reversed it
39th Amendment made it final; 42nd Amendment reversed it
42nd Amendment made it final; 44th Amendment reversed it
44th Amendment made it final; 38th Amendment reversed it
x: The 38th Amendment of 1975 made the President’s satisfaction final, while the 44th Amendment reversed that position.
tq: Pair the two Amendments with opposite effects and check their chronological order.
sec: Ordinance - Article 123, life, lapse, review cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The Supreme Court in D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1987) held that:
o: Every Ordinance automatically becomes a constitutional amendment
Routine re-promulgation of Ordinances without placing them before the legislature is a fraud on the Constitution
The President’s satisfaction is never subject to review
An Ordinance must remain in force for at least six months
x: D.C. Wadhwa held that routine re-promulgation without placing the Ordinance before the legislature amounts to a fraud on the Constitution.
tq: Match the case with its distinctive holding and avoid importing the later case’s broader formulation.
sec: Ordinance - Article 123, life, lapse, review cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which of the following was held in Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (2017)?
o: The Ordinance-making power was held to be a power to amend the Constitution
Re-promulgation is always valid if the executive considers it necessary
A seven-judge Bench held re-promulgation unconstitutional, made laying before the House mandatory and treated satisfaction as justiciable
The President alone may decide whether an Ordinance should be laid before the House
x: The seven-judge Bench in Krishna Kumar Singh held that re-promulgation is unconstitutional, laying the Ordinance before the House is mandatory, and the satisfaction is justiciable.
tq: Use the case-name-to-holding method and identify the option containing all three linked holdings.
sec: Ordinance - Article 123, life, lapse, review cases  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the absolute veto of the President of India?
o: Keeping a Bill pending without deciding on it
Returning an Ordinary Bill for reconsideration once
Overriding a Bill by a higher majority in Parliament
x: Absolute veto means withholding assent to a Bill. It may apply to Private Members’ Bills and Government Bills when the Council of Ministers has resigned before assent.
tq: Distinguish the three forms of presidential veto by their operative effect: withhold, return or keep pending.
sec: ■ Veto types → Bills  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The absolute veto of the President may ordinarily be exercised in respect of which of the following?
o: Private Members’ Bills and Government Bills when the Cabinet has resigned before assent
Bills passed by a State Legislature only
x: The absolute veto involves withholding assent and is relevant to Private Members’ Bills and Government Bills when the Cabinet resigns before assent.
tq: Match the veto with the specific class of Bills to which it applies, while rejecting extreme alternatives such as ‘alone’.
sec: ■ Veto types → Bills  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the suspensive veto of the President:
1. It involves returning a Bill for reconsideration once.
2. If the Bill is passed again, the President must give assent.
3. It is available in respect of Money Bills.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: A suspensive veto permits the President to return an Ordinary Bill once for reconsideration. If Parliament passes it again, assent becomes mandatory. This veto does not apply to Money Bills.
tq: Find the single wrong statement by testing the important Money Bill exception.
sec: ■ Veto types → Bills  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: With reference to the pocket veto of the President of India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It can be exercised only for a period of six months.
It permits the President to return a Money Bill for reconsideration.
It keeps an Ordinary Bill pending without any constitutional time limit for decision.
It is a veto that can be overridden by a two-thirds majority of Parliament.
x: Pocket veto means keeping a Bill pending without taking a decision. The Constitution prescribes no time limit for the President to act in this manner, and it applies to Ordinary Bills.
tq: Separate pocket veto from suspensive veto by focusing on the absence of a constitutional time limit.
sec: ■ Veto types → Bills  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the qualified veto in the Indian constitutional system?
o: It involves the possibility of overriding the veto through a specified stronger majority.
It can be overridden by a higher majority.
It is recognised as a veto available to the President of India.
It is conceptually different from an absolute veto.
x: Qualified veto is an overridable veto by a higher majority, but it is not available to the President of India. Therefore, its recognition as an Indian presidential power is incorrect.
tq: Identify the exception by separating a general constitutional concept from the power actually available in India.
sec: ■ Veto types → Bills  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the case of a Money Bill, the President may either give assent or withhold assent.
2. The President may return a Money Bill for reconsideration under the suspensive veto.
3. The President is constitutionally bound to give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The President may assent to or withhold assent to a Money Bill but cannot return it for reconsideration. Under the Twenty-Fourth Amendment, assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill is mandatory.
tq: Use the Bill-type distinction: Money Bills cannot be returned, whereas Constitutional Amendment Bills require assent.
sec: ■ Veto types → Bills  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The constitutional requirement that the President must give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill is associated with the:
x: The Twenty-Fourth Constitutional Amendment made it obligatory for the President to give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill duly passed by Parliament.
tq: Use the amendment-number trap by linking the specific constitutional change to the correct amendment.
sec: ■ Veto types → Bills  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: The Eleventh Constitutional Amendment of 1961 is associated with which of the following changes?
o: Removal of nominated members from the Vice-Presidential electoral college
Providing for election of the Vice-President by State Legislatures
Ending the joint-meeting method for the election of the Vice-President
Introduction of direct election to the office of Vice-President
x: The Eleventh Amendment ended the earlier joint-meeting method and provided for election of the Vice-President by the members of both Houses of Parliament.
tq: Test the amendment by identifying the precise institutional procedure it altered, not the broader office concerned.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s: Jagdeep Dhankhar’s resignation as Vice-President in July 2025 and the subsequent election of C. P. Radhakrishnan are relevant primarily to which constitutional provisions?
x: Articles 65 and 68 deal respectively with the Vice-President acting as President and the filling of a vacancy in the office of Vice-President. The July 2025 resignation therefore invoked these provisions.
tq: Use the office-function pairing: identify the Articles dealing with acting arrangements and a Vice-Presidential vacancy.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s: C. P. Radhakrishnan became Vice-President of India after the resignation of Jagdeep Dhankhar. This was described as the:
o: First mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President
Second mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President
Third mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President
Fourth mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President
x: The resignation of Jagdeep Dhankhar and the election of C. P. Radhakrishnan constituted the third mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President.
tq: Treat the ordinal number as a direct quantitative fact and reject nearby sequential distractors.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the tenure of the President of India:
1. The Constitution prescribes no limit on the number of terms that a person may serve as President.
2. India follows an informal convention limiting the President to two terms.
3. The two-term limit is expressly imposed by a constitutional amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Constitution does not prescribe a term limit for the President, although an informal convention of two terms is discussed. No constitutional amendment expressly imposes such a limit.
tq: Distinguish a constitutional rule from an informal convention and reject the amendment trap.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s: Which of the following correctly states the comparison concerning presidential term limits?
o: The United States permits only one presidential term, whereas South Korea permits two five-year terms.
The United States limits a President to two terms, whereas South Korea provides for a single five-year term.
Both the United States and South Korea prescribe two presidential terms.
Both the United States and South Korea prescribe a single five-year presidential term.
x: The Twenty-Second Amendment of the United States limits a President to two terms. South Korea follows a single five-year presidential term.
tq: Handle comparison questions by checking both parts of the pair rather than recognising only one correct country.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s: N. Sanjiva Reddy is associated with which one of the following distinctions?
o: Being the first Vice-President of India
Being the first nominated President of India
Being the only President of India elected unopposed
Being the first President elected directly by the people
x: N. Sanjiva Reddy holds the distinction of being the only President of India elected unopposed. He was elected President in 1977.
tq: Use the unique-distinction clue and reject options that confuse presidential and vice-presidential election methods.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s: President Droupadi Murmu promulgated the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026. What change did the Ordinance provide?
o: Increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 33 to 37, excluding the CJI
Increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 37 to 40, excluding the CJI
Increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 33 to 37, including the CJI
Increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 31 to 33, excluding the CJI
x: The 2026 Ordinance increased the number of Supreme Court judges from 33 to 37, with the Chief Justice of India excluded from this count.
tq: Separate the numerical change from the counting exception relating to the Chief Justice of India.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 was gazetted on:
x: The Ordinance was gazetted on 16 May 2026. The other dates relate to reports or commentary rather than the gazette date.
tq: Distinguish the official notification date from later reporting and criticism dates.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s: The President addresses both Houses of Parliament assembled together at the commencement of the Budget Session under:
x: Article 87 provides for the President’s special address to both Houses assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election and the first session of each year, including the Budget Session context.
tq: Use the Article-number distinction among provisions dealing with parliamentary sessions, participation and ordinances.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Election method of the President of India — United States
Impeachment procedure of the President of India — Ireland
Election method of the President of India — Ireland
Impeachment procedure of the President of India — South Korea
x: The method of election of the President of India was borrowed from Ireland, whereas the impeachment procedure was borrowed from the United States.
tq: Start with the sure borrowing pair and guard against swapping the sources of election and impeachment.
sec: ■ Universal angles

s: Epuru Sudhakar is associated with which constitutional issue?
x: The 2006 Epuru Sudhakar case concerned judicial review of the exercise of the pardoning power. It is associated with the constitutional limits on clemency decisions.
tq: Link the case name with its distinctive constitutional power instead of the office or emergency provisions.
